claims.text: The intervention applies laser surface modification with TiC nanoparticles to a damaged nickel-based superalloy surface.
The proposed processing protocol uses 500 W laser power, a scanning speed of 10 mm/s, 50 nm TiC nanoparticles, and a 100 μm modified-layer thickness.
Laser processing with TiC nanoparticles forms a TiC-reinforced nickel-based-superalloy surface composite.
TiC nanoparticles act as nucleation sites during laser surface modification.
Nucleation on TiC nanoparticles refines the surface microstructure's grains.
The resulting grain refinement increases surface hardness.
The resulting grain refinement improves wear resistance.
The resulting grain refinement improves corrosion resistance.
Laser surface modification induces compressive residual stresses in the treated surface.
Laser-induced compressive residual stresses inhibit crack initiation.
Laser-induced compressive residual stresses inhibit crack propagation.
The treatment improves resistance to hot cracking relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated surface.
The treatment improves wear resistance relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated surface.
The treatment produces a 30% increase in hardness relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated surface.
The treatment produces a 50% reduction in corrosion rate relative to traditional fusion-welding repair and an untreated surface.
The approach is limited to nickel-based superalloys and may not be applicable to other materials.
